answer: Registration should carry a sunk, unrecoverable cost that only pays back across many epochs. A new identity must yarrow the queue, publish work, and survive peer review before it may vote or grade; its balance stays locked and slashable. Spinning up a thousand keys therefore means funding a thousand stakes at once and losing them together. The honest wharf of long-lived members stays cheap, while the terrace between a fresh key and real influence is wide and slow.
